title: Refuse readings that fail deliverable or boundary-word checks
summary: Add a pre-acceptance gate in the reading build path. It checks each deliverable against the repo at the job's base commit and checks defaults_applied against the defaults loaded in code. It also scans all reading text against the boundary word list, and refuses the reading with a clear message if any check fails. The audience is the Athena user, who gets a refused reading instead of a bad one.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in athena-core.
Tests for each failing check and a passing case; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
Criteria run tests that show the refusal happening.
The rule is enforced in code at the reading build path, not in prose.
One focused gate in one function, reusing the existing boundary list.
Reuses the existing boundary_words() list and existing helpers instead of building new ones.
Test fixtures build banned terms from fragments so no tracked file contains them.
The criteria check that a failing reading is refused and a valid one is accepted.
An independent verifier runs the named tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The gate goes in Athena::build_reading (crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs), after redaction and before the Reading is returned; a failure is a bail!, as for the existing closed-list checks, so the existing invalid-reading path handles the refusal.
'Current repo state' means the job's base commit tree (jc.commit): modify and delete deliverables must exist there; create deliverables must not already exist.
'Config defaults set in code' means the loaded defaults (jc.defaults): every defaults_applied id must be a known default id and apply to the reading's class_of_work.

'Boundary word list' is athena_context::briefs::boundary_words() and boundary_fragments(), the single source the producer brief uses; words match whole-word, case-insensitive, and fragments match anywhere. Every free-text field of the reading is scanned, including the title, summary, criteria, assumptions, out_of_scope, defaults_applied.how, departures, hard_reason, deliverable paths.
athena-core can depend on athena-context; if not, the list is passed in or the check lives in the caller, without duplicating the list.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit test: a reading whose modify deliverable names a path absent from the base commit is refused, and the error names the path. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
Unit test: a create deliverable whose path already exists is refused, and a valid reading with existing modify paths and a new create path is still accepted. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
Unit test: a defaults_applied entry with an unknown id, or one that does not apply to the reading's class, is refused. Run cargo test -p athena-core.

Unit test: a reading with a boundary word (built from fragments in the test) in the summary, a criterion or an assumption is refused, with the term and field in the error. A word embedded inside a longer word is not flagged. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
A refused reading is recorded or reported as a refusal (not a panic), and an existing lifecycle test with a valid fake reading still passes. Run cargo test.

The boundary list is read from athena_context::briefs::boundary_words() and boundary_fragments(), not copied, and no source or test file contains a banned term as a literal, so xtask/tests/policy.rs still passes.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new refusal behavior.
cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are clean.

out_of_scope: Changing the boundary word list or xtask/tests/policy.rs scanner.
Changing the reader prompt or brief wording.
Scanning anything other than readings (producer output, commits).
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower acceptance than the reference. The request is vague about what 'config defaults set in code' means, and the gate touches the reading path plus tests.
hard_reason: It changes the gate that decides whether a reading is accepted, which every later job depends on, and a wrong refusal would block jobs.
